key_researchers.name: Iris Reinhartz-Berger
key_researchers.affiliation: Professor, Department of Information Systems, University of Haifa, Israel

She has already published in the human-LLM co-reasoning space herself (Iterative vs Plan-Driven Approaches in Human-LLM Collaborative Modeling, CAiSE 2026; Leveraging LLMs for Domain Modeling, CAiSE 2025), so SQ1 cannot claim to open the control-handover question - only the move from fixed interaction schedules to uncertainty-specific triggering.

key_researchers.name: Arnon Sturm
key_researchers.affiliation: Department of Software and Information Systems Engineering, Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Israel
key_researchers.connects_to: Cheers/ParkWise corpus design and study protocol; SQ3 transfer argument; regulated-domain analogy for the medical extension
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-supervisor and VEGO-AI co-author. The human-vs-machine domain modelling experiments with Bragilovski and Dalpiaz (RE 2024, REJ 2025, EMSE 2026) are the methodological template for measuring when machine output helps or misleads a human. His ER 2025 legal-domain explainable-AI paper is a direct precedent for taking conceptual-modelling machinery into a regulated domain.

key_researchers.name: Maxim Bragilovski
key_researchers.affiliation: PhD researcher, Department of Software and Information Systems Engineering, Ben-Gurion University of the Negev
key_researchers.verification: Partial - role confirmed, current status not re-confirmed
key_researchers.connects_to: Cheers/ParkWise UML corpus and the four-agent pipeline as inherited infrastructure
key_researchers.why_relevant: VEGO-AI co-author whose empirical pipeline this doctorate inherits. His four-paper arc (REFSQ 2022, RE 2024, REJ 2025, EMSE 2026) is the evidence base showing that machine-produced models sometimes help and sometimes harm novice modellers - which is the empirical justification for making intervention selective rather than uniform.

key_researchers.name: Arava Tsoury
key_researchers.affiliation: University of Haifa, Israel
key_researchers.verification: Partial - co-authorship confirmed, exact current post not confirmed
key_researchers.connects_to: The human-judgment layer's record schema
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-author of the CAiSE 2026 human-LLM collaborative modelling study and of an Information Systems 2025 paper on how humans combine multiple information sources to explain observations - an empirical account of how a person justifies a judgment, which is exactly the raw material a judgment-representation schema must encode. Inside the supervisor's own group, so approach her before looking outside it.

key_researchers.name: Jordi Cabot
key_researchers.affiliation: Head of the Software Engineering RDI Unit, Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST); affiliate professor, University of Luxembourg; FNR PEARL Chair (BESSER)
key_researchers.connects_to: The human-judgment layer's trigger; BESSER as a plausible SQ3 transfer host
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-author of Towards Human-in-the-Loop LLM-Enabled Domain Modeling (ER 2025), the closest published statement of SQ1's problem outside the supervisors' group. It supplies a non-LLM arbiter architecture with uncertainty-ranked question selection but no policy for when to invoke the human at all. Treat as a competitor for the SQ1 novelty claim, not background. Plausible external examiner.

key_researchers.name: Henderik A. (Erik) Proper
key_researchers.affiliation: Full Professor of Enterprise and Process Engineering, Business Informatics Group, TU Wien, Austria (moved from Luxembourg January 2023)
key_researchers.connects_to: SQ3 governance framing; legitimacy of carrying a modelling judgment between organisational contexts
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-author of the ER 2025 human-in-the-loop LLM domain modelling paper and a long-standing authority on the foundations of domain modelling in enterprise contexts. He is the person best placed to challenge or endorse the claim that guideline operationalisation transfers across contexts.

key_researchers.name: Dominik Bork
key_researchers.affiliation: Associate Professor, leads the Business Informatics Group, Institute of Information Systems Engineering, TU Wien, Austria
key_researchers.connects_to: SQ2 - reconciling judgments captured at different views and granularities
key_researchers.why_relevant: Direct co-author of the primary supervisor (Reinhartz-Berger, Ali, Bork, CAiSE 2025 on LLM granularity and strategy in domain modelling). The natural external bridge between the Haifa variability line and the Vienna conceptual-modelling line; shares a group with Proper. His multi-view modelling and model-consistency work supplies machinery for reconciling judgments without collapsing them.

key_researchers.name: Syed Juned Ali
key_researchers.affiliation: Business Informatics Group, TU Wien, Austria
key_researchers.connects_to: The human-judgment layer; a reusable interaction dataset for a Study 1 pilot
key_researchers.why_relevant: Lead author of How are LLMs Used for Conceptual Modeling? (ER 2024) and of the associated annotated prompt event-log dataset - the most directly reusable SQ1 data asset in this reference set, because it records real human-LLM interaction during conceptual modelling without requiring new expert recruitment.

key_researchers.name: Gunter Mussbacher
key_researchers.affiliation: Associate Professor, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, McGill University, Montreal, Canada
key_researchers.connects_to: The Model Inspector agent; the substantial-vs-occasional distinction
key_researchers.why_relevant: Runs the closest competing programme on automated model assessment (Automated Domain Modeling with LLMs: A Comparative Study, MODELS 2023; Embedding-based Automated Assessment of Domain Models, MODELS Companion 2024; Detecting mistakes in a domain model, MODELS Companion 2022). His mistake-detection work assumes 'mistake' is well defined, which is exactly what the occasional-variability category problematises. His comparative protocol is the yardstick SQ3 will be measured against.

key_researchers.name: Daniel (Daniel) Varro
key_researchers.affiliation: Professor of Software Engineering, McGill University; also Linkoping University, Sweden; co-founder of IncQuery Labs
key_researchers.verification: Partial - genuinely multi-site, reported differently across sources
key_researchers.connects_to: SQ2's 'unsafe generalization' detector; consistency of a model after a reused judgment is applied
key_researchers.why_relevant: Senior author on the MODELS 2023 comparative study and the embedding-based assessment work. His formal machinery for consistency checking and automatic generation of consistent models is the rigour anchor for verifying that reusing a stored judgment does not introduce inconsistency into the target model.

key_researchers.name: Boqi (Percy) Chen
key_researchers.affiliation: PhD 2025, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, McGill University (supervised by Mussbacher and Varro)
key_researchers.verification: Verified this session (McGill ECE PhD defence announcement and personal page)
key_researchers.connects_to: The Model Inspector agent; the nearest published analogue of an LLM judging model correctness
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-author of the MODELS 2023 comparative study, the embedding-based assessment paper, the multi-step iterative domain modelling paper, and MCeT: Behavioral Model Correctness Evaluation using LLMs (MODELS 2025). MCeT is the baseline any claim about LLM-based model assessment quality must acknowledge.

key_researchers.name: Kua Chen
key_researchers.affiliation: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, McGill University, Canada
key_researchers.verification: Partial - group affiliation confirmed this session, current status not confirmed
key_researchers.connects_to: The Cheers/ParkWise corpus treated as an assessment corpus; a natural ablation baseline
key_researchers.why_relevant: Lead author of Automated Domain Modeling with Large Language Models: A Comparative Study (MODELS 2023) and of Embedding-based Automated Assessment of Domain Models (MODELS Companion 2024). Embedding-based assessment is the mechanical alternative to VEGO-AI's agentic reasoning, so it is the obvious cheap baseline a reviewer will ask about.

key_researchers.name: Yujing Yang
key_researchers.affiliation: McGill University, Canada
key_researchers.verification: Partial - group affiliation confirmed this session
key_researchers.connects_to: The multi-agent iteration pattern behind the four VEGO-AI agents

Lead author of Multi-step Iterative Automated Domain Modeling with Large Language Models (MODELS Companion 2024) and co-author of the 2023 comparative study and the embedding-based assessment paper. Fix the name before it enters any supervisor-facing document.

key_researchers.name: Jorg Kienzle
key_researchers.affiliation: School of Computer Science, McGill University, Montreal, Canada
key_researchers.connects_to: The substantial-vs-occasional distinction; the reuse semantics of the human-judgment layer
key_researchers.why_relevant: Owns the reference-solution automated grading line (Automated Grading of Class Diagrams, MODELS-C 2019; Is automated grading of models effective?, MODELS 2020) whose single-correct-answer assumption this doctorate replaces with governed expert judgment. Separately, with Alam and Mussbacher he originated Concern-Oriented Reuse, which already treats a variability decision as a first-class deferrable reusable artifact - a Tier-2-style mechanism inside a Tier-1 person.

key_researchers.name: Omar Alam
key_researchers.affiliation: Department of Computing and Information Systems, Trent University, Peterborough, Canada (NOT Concordia or McGill; PhD at McGill)
key_researchers.verification: Partial (workbook explicitly corrects the common affiliation error)
key_researchers.connects_to: SQ2 - the boundary between structural reuse and governed reuse
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-author of both grading papers and lead author of Modelling a family of systems for crisis management with concern-oriented reuse (SPE 2017). CORE is the reference point for how far reuse of modelling decisions can be pushed by structure alone, and therefore where governance - validation, reconciliation, retained human authority - has to take over. Closest structural analogue and clearest contrast case at once.

key_researchers.name: Weiyi Bian
key_researchers.affiliation: UNCERTAIN - associated with the Alam/Kienzle grading line; reported variously against Trent University and McGill
key_researchers.verification: Uncertain - affiliation not confirmed this session

key_researchers.why_relevant: Lead author of both Automated Grading of Class Diagrams (MODELS-C 2019) and Is automated grading of models effective? (MODELS 2020), the latter empirically evaluated on real undergraduate cohorts of 103 and 89 students. This is the closest existing study design to the corpus the thesis uses, and its assumption is the one the thesis overturns.

key_researchers.name: Maria Blanca Ibanez
key_researchers.affiliation: Universidad Carlos III de Madrid, Leganes, Spain
key_researchers.connects_to: SQ1's escalation trigger - which failure class should raise a request
key_researchers.why_relevant: Lead author of Can Multimodal Large Language Models Grade Like an Expert? (Computer Applications in Engineering Education, 2025). Her finding that multimodal LLMs fail specifically on semantic interpretation and evaluative reasoning is the most directly usable empirical justification for escalating on interpretation rather than on syntax.

key_researchers.name: Nacir Bouali (with Faizan Ahmed)
key_researchers.affiliation: University of Twente, Netherlands

key_researchers.connects_to: SQ1 - mixed-initiative assessment where the instructor retains authority
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-author of Toward Automated UML Diagram Assessment: Comparing LLM-Generated Scores with Teaching Assistants (CSEDU 2025) and of a 2026 follow-up found in this session (Beyond Grading Accuracy: Exploring Alignment of TAs and LLMs, arXiv:2603.16357) that analyses 92 diagrams with six open-source LLMs at criterion level and explicitly frames the result as support for mixed-initiative grading with instructor oversight. New prior art not yet in the workbook - add and verify the venue.

key_researchers.name: Lola Burgueno
key_researchers.affiliation: Associate Professor, University of Malaga (Atenea group / ITIS Software), Spain
key_researchers.connects_to: Study 1's evaluation design; the definition of 'important uncertainty' in the human-judgment layer
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-author of On the Utility of Domain Modeling Assistance with Large Language Models (MAGDA, ACM TOSEM 2026), a rigorous user study of whether LLM modelling assistance actually helps - the evaluation design Study 1 should replicate, redirected from suggestion quality to intervention triggering. Her separate uncertainty-management line gives SQ1 a formal vocabulary. She is also General Chair of MODELS 2026, the venue of the base paper.

key_researchers.name: Houari Sahraoui
key_researchers.affiliation: Professor, GEODES lab, DIRO, Universite de Montreal, Canada; Vice-Dean, Faculty of Arts and Sciences
key_researchers.connects_to: The evaluation story - the strongest adversary for the thesis's claims
key_researchers.why_relevant: Senior author on MAGDA and on the few-shot prompt learning for model completion line. Thirty years of automating and evaluating software development makes him the person most likely to ask whether the governed-judgment layer actually beats a well-tuned fully automatic baseline. SQ3's design should pre-empt exactly that comparison.

key_researchers.name: Istvan David
key_researchers.affiliation: Assistant Professor, McMaster University, Canada; leads the Sustainable Systems and Methods Lab; McMaster Centre for Software Certification (McSCert)
key_researchers.connects_to: SQ2's reconciliation problem; a software-side analogue of regulated-domain governance for the medical extension
key_researchers.why_relevant: MAGDA co-author with a PhD on model consistency management in multi-paradigm settings. His consistency work is directly reusable when stored judgments conflict, and the McSCert certification context is the closest software-side analogue of the governance regime a healthcare arm would need. An early-career collaborator rather than an examiner.

key_researchers.name: Fabiano Dalpiaz
key_researchers.affiliation: Professor of Software Production, Utrecht University, Netherlands; PI of the RE lab; Editor-in-Chief of Springer's Requirements Engineering; Steering Committee chair of REFSQ
key_researchers.connects_to: The corpus and study protocol; publication routing for SQ1 and SQ2
key_researchers.why_relevant: Already a co-author of both Sturm and Bragilovski (REFSQ 2022, RE 2024, REJ 2025, EMSE 2026), so effectively part of the extended supervisory network. His stated focus on the synergies of AI and humans for building trustworthy software is the closest existing statement of the umbrella question in the RE community, and he gatekeeps the two most natural outlets.

key_researchers.name: Hoa Khanh Dam
key_researchers.affiliation: Professor and Deputy Head of School (Research), University of Wollongong, Australia
key_researchers.connects_to: The four-agent architecture; SQ2's gap statement
key_researchers.why_relevant: Sole author of Towards Multi-Agentic AI for automated software design and modelling (ASEW 2025), which explicitly names conflict and inconsistency reconciliation across agent-produced design models as an open challenge. This is the clearest external statement of the SQ2 gap - cite it so the gap is community-recognised rather than self-declared.

key_researchers.name: Qin Ma and Pierre Kelsen
key_researchers.affiliation: University of Luxembourg (co-authors with first author Jonathan Silva Mercado)
key_researchers.connects_to: The specific mechanism SQ1 must build on or differentiate from
key_researchers.why_relevant: The Luxembourg group behind the ER 2025 rule-based moderator and uncertainty-ranked question selection. Worth monitoring for a journal extension that could close more of SQ1 before the thesis does.

key_researchers.name: Hussein Mozannar
key_researchers.affiliation: MIT (Clinical Machine Learning group / Institute for Data, Systems and Society), USA
key_researchers.connects_to: The trigger between the Variability Explorer and the human-judgment layer
key_researchers.why_relevant: Most consistent author on the modern learning-to-defer line (ICML 2020 consistent surrogates; AISTATS 2023 exact algorithms; a human-AI deferral benchmark). His formulations and released code are the most likely direct baseline for SQ1's escalation policy - read them for what they assume about the expert.

key_researchers.name: David Sontag
key_researchers.affiliation: MIT (Clinical Machine Learning Group, CSAIL), USA
key_researchers.connects_to: SQ1 implementation; a healthcare bridge for SQ3 (read-ahead only - Plan A passes 0 of 6 gates)
key_researchers.why_relevant: Senior author on the deferral line and its clinical framing. The group's publication record and public repositories give SQ1 reusable implementations, and the clinical framing is the safest way to read ahead on the medical extension without making any clinical claim.

key_researchers.name: Ran El-Yaniv
key_researchers.affiliation: Technion - Israel Institute of Technology
key_researchers.connects_to: How Study 1 reports results without needing an accuracy headline
key_researchers.why_relevant: Foundational author on selective classification (JMLR 2010 with Wiener; NeurIPS 2017 with Geifman). The risk-coverage framing - accuracy as a function of the fraction of cases handled without a human - is the reporting instrument SQ1 should adopt, and it is compatible with the current zero-expert-label position because it is a design commitment rather than a result.

key_researchers.name: Yonatan Geifman
key_researchers.affiliation: Technion at the time of the 2017 work; current position uncertain (widely reported to have moved to industry)
key_researchers.connects_to: The concrete wrapper implementation for a coverage-controlled trigger
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-author of Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks (NeurIPS 2017) and its practical SGR procedure - the closest thing to an off-the-shelf mechanism for guaranteeing a target risk at a chosen coverage level, which is the operational form of 'without unnecessary expert burden'.

key_researchers.name: Mehryar Mohri
key_researchers.affiliation: Google Research and Courant Institute, New York University, USA
key_researchers.connects_to: SQ1's objective function under a bounded expert-attention constraint
key_researchers.why_relevant: Theory backbone from Learning with Rejection (ALT 2016) through Budgeted Multiple-Expert Deferral (2025). The budgeted work is the most current formal treatment of the constraint that expert attention is finite - which is what turns 'without unnecessary expert burden' from an aspiration into a specifiable objective.

key_researchers.name: Jesse Davis
key_researchers.affiliation: KU Leuven, Belgium (DTAI)
key_researchers.connects_to: The internal structure of the trigger - two distinct escalation channels
key_researchers.why_relevant: Senior author of the Machine Learning (2024) reject-option survey. Its ambiguity-versus-novelty rejection taxonomy maps directly onto two different reasons to escalate: 'the four agents disagree' versus 'this case is unlike anything the system has seen', which should not share a threshold.

key_researchers.name: Yarin Gal
key_researchers.affiliation: University of Oxford, OATML, UK
key_researchers.connects_to: The four agents specifically - avoiding escalation on mere wording differences
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-author of Semantic Uncertainty (ICLR 2023). Meaning-level rather than token-level agreement is what stops the system escalating when two agents expressed the same judgment in different words - a concrete and necessary component of any multi-agent disagreement trigger.

key_researchers.name: Lucy Lu Wang
key_researchers.affiliation: University of Washington, USA
key_researchers.connects_to: The U-RQ's 'governed' clause
key_researchers.why_relevant: Senior author of Know Your Limits: A Survey of Abstention in Large Language Models (TACL 2025). Its epistemic-versus-normative abstention distinction is what allows SQ1 to be framed as governance - some escalations happen because the system does not know, others because it is not the system's place to decide - rather than as pure uncertainty handling.

key_researchers.name: Anirudha Majumdar
key_researchers.affiliation: Princeton University, USA
key_researchers.connects_to: The formal statement of SQ1 in full: important uncertainties addressed, expert burden minimised
key_researchers.why_relevant: Senior author of KnowNo / Robots That Ask For Help (CoRL 2023) - conformal-prediction-calibrated help-seeking by an LLM planner with a minimised help rate and a task-success guarantee. This is the closest existing end-to-end template for what SQ1 is trying to build, in a different application domain.

key_researchers.name: Burr Settles
key_researchers.affiliation: University of Wisconsin-Madison at the time of the 2009 survey; current position uncertain (widely reported to be in industry research)
key_researchers.connects_to: The trigger's candidate-selection policies
key_researchers.why_relevant: Author of the canonical Active Learning Literature Survey (2009) - the catalogue of query strategies (uncertainty sampling, query-by-committee, expected model change). Important caveat to state explicitly: active learning selects examples to improve a model, whereas SQ1 selects cases to resolve a judgment; borrowing the framing wholesale would misdescribe the contribution.

key_researchers.name: Eric Horvitz
key_researchers.affiliation: Microsoft, Chief Scientific Officer, USA (exact 2026 title not independently re-confirmed)
key_researchers.connects_to: The derivation of the triggering criterion itself
key_researchers.why_relevant: Principles of Mixed-Initiative User Interfaces (CHI 1999) is the theoretical origin of SQ1: weigh the uncertainty of the user's goals against the expected utility of acting versus asking, and take initiative only when automation's expected value exceeds leaving control with the human. Any credible SQ1 chapter derives from, or argues explicitly against, this framing. Also a co-author on the CHI 2019 guidelines.

key_researchers.name: Saleema Amershi
key_researchers.affiliation: Partner Research Manager, Microsoft Research AI Frontiers (leads the teams behind AutoGen and Magentic-One), Redmond, USA
key_researchers.connects_to: The four agents; the interaction design of an intervention request; preservation of human authority inside an agent team
key_researchers.why_relevant: First author of the 18 Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction (CHI 2019), the design vocabulary for what a well-governed intervention request looks like - make clear what the system can do, scope services when in doubt, support efficient correction and dismissal. Her multi-agent platform work is the closest industrial analogue to VEGO-AI's four-agent architecture.

key_researchers.name: Eduardo Mosqueira-Rey
key_researchers.affiliation: Universidade da Coruna, Spain
key_researchers.connects_to: The Chapter 2 positioning sentence for the human-judgment layer
key_researchers.why_relevant: Lead author of the AI Review (2023) human-in-the-loop ML state of the art. Its control-locus taxonomy - active learning, interactive ML, machine teaching - is the standard vocabulary for positioning governed human judgment between system-driven and expert-driven loops.

key_researchers.name: Andreas Metzger
key_researchers.affiliation: Senior researcher, Software Systems Engineering, University of Duisburg-Essen and paluno - The Ruhr Institute for Software Technology, Germany
key_researchers.connects_to: A ready-made, empirically validated triggering formalism for SQ1; also Tier 3 via the SPL line
key_researchers.why_relevant: Mechanically the most useful person on this list for SQ1. Proactive Process Adaptation Using Deep Learning Ensembles (CAiSE 2019) uses per-prediction reliability estimates to decide the earliest moment an automated action is trustworthy enough to fire - structurally identical to deciding when an agentic assessor should stop and ask. His TAAS 2024 user study on explainable online RL supplies the human-facing evaluation half.

key_researchers.name: Stefanie Rinderle-Ma
key_researchers.affiliation: Technical University of Munich (TUM), Chair of Information Systems and Business Process Management, Germany
key_researchers.connects_to: The shape of the human-judgment request; a cross-domain (process) bridge for SQ3
key_researchers.why_relevant: Senior author of Conversational Process Modelling (BPM Forum 2023). Her group is the leading source on dialogue-based elicitation between systems and domain experts - the interaction-design half of SQ1. Placed in Tier 2 rather than Tier 1 because what the thesis takes is the mechanism, and BPM is a transfer context rather than the home setting.

key_researchers.name: Jessica S. Ancker
key_researchers.affiliation: Vanderbilt University Medical Center, USA (the study was conducted at Weill Cornell Medicine)
key_researchers.connects_to: A state-dependent interruption cost - the piece the deferral literature lacks; also touches the medical extension
key_researchers.why_relevant: Author of the definitive quantitative alert-fatigue study (BMC MIDM 2017): override rates rise with workload and repeated alerts. This is the empirical basis for making the cost of interrupting an expert depend on their current state - a genuine and defensible contribution opening for SQ1 that requires no clinical data and no Plan A gate.

key_researchers.name: Lora Aroyo
key_researchers.affiliation: Research Scientist and team lead (Data Excellence for Evaluating Responsibly), Google DeepMind / Google Research, USA
key_researchers.connects_to: The substantial-vs-occasional distinction head-on; the EXP-005 label protocol; the judgment store's conflict semantics
key_researchers.why_relevant: The central figure for SQ2's hardest assumption. CrowdTruth (AI Magazine 2015) and the later DICES/DIVE datasets argue that annotator disagreement is signal, not noise, and that a single gold standard is the wrong target. Applied here: when two experts disagree about whether a difference is substantial or occasional, the store must preserve that rather than silently resolving it.

key_researchers.name: Barbara Plank
key_researchers.affiliation: LMU Munich / Munich Center for Machine Learning (MCML), Germany
key_researchers.connects_to: How SQ2 stores multi-expert judgment; the human-agreement ceiling for SQ3 transfer experiments
key_researchers.why_relevant: Author of the human label variation position paper (EMNLP 2022) and co-author of Learning from Disagreement (JAIR 2021). The human-agreement ceiling is the honest denominator for any future EXP-005 analysis, and the reason a naive accuracy target would be the wrong instrument even once labels exist.

key_researchers.name: Federico Cabitza
key_researchers.affiliation: University of Milano-Bicocca, Italy (uncertain - not confirmed this session)
key_researchers.connects_to: The EXP-005 labelling protocol design
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-author of Toward a Perspectivist Turn in Ground Truthing for Predictive Computing (AAAI 2023). The perspectivist position reframes the 0-of-24 label situation as a design question about what a label should be, rather than only a data shortfall - useful for writing the protocol before the labels arrive.

key_researchers.name: Massimo Poesio
key_researchers.affiliation: Queen Mary University of London, UK (uncertain - not confirmed this session)
key_researchers.connects_to: The agreement statistics the expert-labelling protocol will report
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-author of Learning from Disagreement (JAIR 2021) and of the standard inter-coder agreement survey (Computational Linguistics 2008). Supplies the statistics vocabulary the labelling protocol must commit to in advance so that later results cannot be accused of post-hoc metric selection.

key_researchers.name: Pang Wei Koh
key_researchers.affiliation: University of Washington, USA (Stanford at the time of the WILDS paper); current affiliation not directly confirmed
key_researchers.connects_to: SQ3's evaluation backbone; makes E12's domain-specific vs broadly-transferable distinction operational
key_researchers.why_relevant: Lead author of WILDS (ICML 2021). The in-distribution vs out-of-distribution reporting convention and the domain-generalisation / subpopulation-shift split give SQ3 a precise vocabulary for the distinction Arnon demanded between a domain-specific uncertainty and a general capability gap.

key_researchers.name: Sayash Kapoor
key_researchers.affiliation: Princeton University, USA (consistent with the research portal record; not directly confirmed)
key_researchers.connects_to: Leakage controls over the Cheers/ParkWise corpus
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-author of Leakage and the reproducibility crisis in machine-learning-based science (Patterns 2023). The eight-type leakage taxonomy and the model info sheet template are the most directly reusable methodology artifacts for SQ3 - and with two domains and two diagram languages, cross-split leakage is a live and specific threat, not a generic one.

key_researchers.name: Arvind Narayanan
key_researchers.affiliation: Princeton University, USA (not directly confirmed)
key_researchers.connects_to: The sceptical-reader persona every results sentence must survive
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-author of the leakage and reproducibility work and a prominent critic of over-claimed ML evaluation. Given the 0-of-24 expert-label position, writing every SQ3 evaluation sentence against this persona is the most practical guard against the project's main failure mode.

key_researchers.name: Thomas Zimmermann
key_researchers.affiliation: Microsoft Research at the time of the 2009 study; later University of California, Irvine (current affiliation not confirmed)
key_researchers.connects_to: SQ3's governance gate - predicting transferability rather than assuming it
key_researchers.why_relevant: Lead author of Cross-project defect prediction: a large scale experiment on data vs domain vs process (ESEC/FSE 2009), the key SE precedent for learning WHEN transfer is advisable rather than assuming it. key_researchers.name: Rogardt Heldal
key_researchers.affiliation: Western Norway University of Applied Sciences, Norway
key_researchers.connects_to: The validity chapter; the strongest counter-position to SQ3
key_researchers.why_relevant: Sole author of Is generalisation hindering the adoption of your findings? (ESEM 2024), based on a failed variability-management artifact across five organisations - the closest published counter-position to SQ3's default assumption, in the same problem domain. Cite him against yourself; it is stronger than being cited by an examiner.

key_researchers.name: Annibale Panichella
key_researchers.affiliation: Delft University of Technology (TU Delft), Netherlands
key_researchers.connects_to: The reporting standard SQ3's evaluation must meet; GPT-4o version drift as a recorded threat
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-author of Breaking the Silence: the Threats of Using LLMs in Software Engineering (ICSE-NIER 2024). He is leading the methodological conversation about how LLM-based SE studies should be designed and reported, which is the bar an examining panel will apply to any VEGO-AI experiment.

key_researchers.name: Ewout W. Steyerberg
key_researchers.affiliation: Erasmus MC, Rotterdam, Netherlands (affiliation as listed on the 2016 paper; current post not re-confirmed)
key_researchers.connects_to: Study 3's design using only the existing corpus
key_researchers.why_relevant: Originator, with Frank Harrell, of the internal / internal-external / external validation hierarchy. Internal-external (leave-one-cluster-out) validation is the most practical transfer design available here - leave-one-domain-out across Cheers and ParkWise, leave-one-language-out across class and use-case diagrams - and it needs no new dataset and no medical gate.

key_researchers.name: Gary S. Collins
key_researchers.affiliation: University of Oxford, Centre for Statistics in Medicine, UK (inferred from TRIPOD authorship, not directly confirmed)
key_researchers.connects_to: The reporting standard a healthcare arm would have to satisfy; transplantable to the software side now
key_researchers.why_relevant: Lead author of TRIPOD and TRIPOD+AI. Sets the reporting bar for any clinical prediction claim - relevant as read-ahead only, since Plan A passes 0 of 6 entry gates. His mandatory-context-disclosure framing can be adopted on the software side immediately without any clinical commitment.

key_researchers.name: Alan R. Hevner
key_researchers.affiliation: University of South Florida, Muma College of Business, USA
key_researchers.connects_to: The artifact / relevance / rigour framing of the whole thesis
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-author of the 2004 MISQ guidelines, sole author of the three-cycle view, co-author of Gregor and Hevner (2013) and Baskerville et al. (2018). The single most-cited voice in DSR and the frame an examiner will implicitly benchmark the methodology chapter against. His recent work with vom Brocke and Maedche covers DSR in AI-augmented settings.

key_researchers.name: Ken Peffers
key_researchers.affiliation: University of Nevada, Las Vegas - Lee Business School, Professor Emeritus of MIS, USA
key_researchers.connects_to: The per-RQ study / artifact / design / evaluation structure Iris required (E13)
key_researchers.why_relevant: Lead author of the DSRM process model that will structure the methodology chapter and the three sub-question iterations. Also a long-standing editorial figure around DESRIST, the natural venue community for a DSR-framed methodological contribution.

key_researchers.name: Shirley Gregor
key_researchers.affiliation: Australian National University, Research School of Management, Australia
key_researchers.connects_to: SQ2's judgment-representation schema; the thesis's contribution-positioning argument
key_researchers.why_relevant: Author of the knowledge contribution framework (Gregor and Hevner 2013), the anatomy of a design theory (Jones and Gregor 2007) and the anatomy of a design principle (Gregor, Kruse and Seidel 2020). The design-principle anatomy is a ready-made schema for storing reusable expert judgment WITH explicit boundary conditions - which is precisely the 'without unsafe generalization' clause of SQ2.

key_researchers.name: Roel J. Wieringa
key_researchers.affiliation: University of Twente, Enschede, Netherlands - Chair of Information Systems, emeritus
key_researchers.connects_to: Chapter 3's gap argument (E4) and Chapter 4's study designs
key_researchers.why_relevant: Author of the SE-facing design science text (2014). His design-problem vs knowledge-question split is the sharpest available tool for Arnon's requirement to separate the proposed agentic solution from the research question. Technical Action Research is a live candidate design for expert-in-the-loop studies where the researcher is also the tool builder.

key_researchers.name: John R. Venable
key_researchers.affiliation: Curtin University, Perth - School of Management and Marketing, Australia
key_researchers.connects_to: Every evaluation-design decision across all three studies
key_researchers.why_relevant: Lead author of FEDS (EJIS 2016), the 2012 comprehensive evaluation framework, and the 2026 MEDS successor. He effectively owns the DSR-evaluation literature; the Human Risk and Effectiveness strategy is the one that fits a human-judgment governance artifact. Still publishing in 2026, so a contemporary rather than a historical citation.

key_researchers.name: Richard Baskerville
key_researchers.affiliation: Georgia State University, Atlanta, USA
key_researchers.connects_to: SQ2's formalisation of expert learning into reusable design knowledge; the defence of an artifact-leaning doctorate
key_researchers.why_relevant: Unusually central because he sits on both methodological lines the thesis needs: co-author of Action Design Research (2011), the precedent for formalising expert learning into reusable design knowledge, and co-author of FEDS/MEDS on evaluation. Also co-author of Baskerville et al. (2018) on the artifact-versus-theory balance.

key_researchers.name: Jan Pries-Heje
key_researchers.affiliation: Roskilde University, Denmark
key_researchers.connects_to: The evaluation strategy chosen for each of the three studies
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-author of FEDS (2016), the 2012 comprehensive evaluation framework, and MEDS (2026). Part of the three-person team that defines how DSR evaluations are designed; read alongside Venable and Baskerville rather than separately.

key_researchers.name: Sandeep Purao
key_researchers.affiliation: Bentley University, Waltham MA, USA
key_researchers.connects_to: The reuse half of the human-judgment layer
key_researchers.why_relevant: ADR co-author and co-author of How Designers Use Design Principles (JAIS 2022). That second strand hits SQ2's blind spot directly: representing and storing expert judgment well is not enough - the thesis must show the judgment is APPLIED appropriately when reused, which is where his application-modes work is the relevant instrument.

key_researchers.name: Matti Rossi
key_researchers.affiliation: Aalto University School of Business, Finland
key_researchers.connects_to: Positioning continuous in-system formalisation of judgment against ADR's end-of-study formalisation
key_researchers.why_relevant: ADR co-author (2011) and co-author of Baskerville et al. (2018). He has also commented on how ADR is being stretched and misapplied (with Sein, EJIS 2019), which is useful when the thesis argues that formalising judgment continuously inside the running system is a different move from ADR's end-of-study formalisation.

key_researchers.name: Maung K. Sein
key_researchers.affiliation: University of Agder, Norway
key_researchers.connects_to: The risk SQ3 exists to manage
key_researchers.why_relevant: Lead author of Action Design Research. His ensemble-artifact premise - that an IT artifact is inseparable from the organisational context that shaped it - is the strongest existing statement of the transfer risk SQ3 is designed to manage. Citing him makes that risk a recognised methodological concern rather than a self-identified weakness.

key_researchers.name: Per Runeson
key_researchers.affiliation: Lund University, Department of Computer Science, Sweden
key_researchers.connects_to: Study 1 and Study 2 empirical protocols
key_researchers.why_relevant: Lead author of the SE case study guidelines (2009) and the 2012 book. Supplies the empirical protocol, unit-of-analysis discipline and validity-threat taxonomy that the DSR literature does not provide, and that the SE half of an examining panel will expect for any study involving modelling experts.

key_researchers.name: Claes Wohlin
key_researchers.affiliation: Blekinge Institute of Technology, Sweden (uncertain - not confirmed this session)
key_researchers.connects_to: Any controlled comparison inside Study 1
key_researchers.why_relevant: Lead author of Experimentation in Software Engineering (2012), the standard SE adaptation of experimental design - the reference for threats-to-validity classification and for designing a controlled comparison of triggering policies if Study 1 takes that form.

key_researchers.name: Jan Recker
key_researchers.affiliation: Nucleus Professor for Information Systems and Digital Innovation, University of Hamburg, Germany; Adjunct at University of Agder and QUT
key_researchers.verification: Verified this session (University of Hamburg Business School pages)
key_researchers.connects_to: The formulation and defence of the research questions themselves (E4, E5, E6)
key_researchers.why_relevant: Author of the standard IS research-methods guide and Senior Editor at MIS Quarterly. His treatment of how to state, scope and defend a research question is the most direct methodological support for the required rewrite of the umbrella RQ - narrowing it to variability identification and classification, and removing reuse into a sub-question.

key_researchers.name: Klaus Pohl
key_researchers.affiliation: Professor, Software Systems Engineering, University of Duisburg-Essen; paluno - The Ruhr Institute for Software Technology, Germany
key_researchers.connects_to: The gap statement: human judgment governance was never on the SPL agenda
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-author of the standard SPLE textbook (2005) and of Software product line engineering and variability management: achievements and challenges (FOSE 2014, with Metzger). He defines the canonical variability vocabulary and the field's research agenda, which makes him the authority to cite when arguing that governance of human judgment was never part of that agenda - a 'why is this open' argument rather than a 'why is my design good' one.

key_researchers.name: Klaus Schmid
key_researchers.affiliation: Professor, Software Systems Engineering, Institute of Computer Science, University of Hildesheim, Germany (previously Fraunhofer IESE)
key_researchers.connects_to: Community-recognised gap positioning for SQ2 and SQ3
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-author of Generative AI And Software Variability - A Research Vision (VaMoS 2024) and of the SPL variability-metrics SLR (IST 2019). The vision paper is the variability community's own statement of the open agenda at the generative-AI intersection - the document to position against so the gap is theirs rather than self-declared. Also active in VARIABILITY 2026, a plausible venue.

key_researchers.name: Thorsten Berger
key_researchers.affiliation: Professor and Chair of Software Engineering, Ruhr University Bochum, Germany; Guest Professor, Chalmers University of Technology and University of Gothenburg, Sweden
key_researchers.connects_to: External-validity check on the substantial-vs-occasional distinction
key_researchers.why_relevant: Leading empiricist on variability in real systems - Linux kernel, Android ecosystems, automotive, robotics - and co-author of the VaMoS 2024 vision. His stance that real variability is messy and only partly intentional is the challenge SQ3 must answer if the substantial/occasional distinction is to hold beyond student UML models.

key_researchers.name: Sven Apel
key_researchers.affiliation: Professor and Chair of Software Engineering, Saarland University / Saarland Informatics Campus, Germany; ERC Advanced Grant holder
key_researchers.connects_to: A design constraint on the trigger: machine uncertainty may not track human difficulty; also the validity chapter
key_researchers.why_relevant: Combines SPL and configurable systems with explicit attention to the human factor, including empirical and neurophysiological methods, and co-authored Views on Internal and External Validity in Empirical SE (ICSE 2015). His recent line testing whether machine uncertainty and human difficulty coincide bears directly on SQ1 - if they do not, model confidence cannot be used as a proxy for 'the human should look at this'. (The specific 2026 ICSE paper on fixation-related potentials and LLM perplexity is reported second-hand in the workbook and was NOT verified this session.)

key_researchers.name: Sofia Ananieva
key_researchers.affiliation: FZI Research Center for Information Technology / Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, Germany
key_researchers.verification: Verified this session - NOTE her dblp record appears under the name Sofia Linsbauer, so search both
key_researchers.connects_to: SQ2's representation substrate - what a judgment is anchored to
key_researchers.why_relevant: Lead author of A conceptual model for unifying variability in space and time (EMSE 2022) and of the KIT monograph on consistent view-based management of variability. A unified conceptual vocabulary for variability is the substrate on which a captured judgment must be anchored if it is to be retrievable and checkable later.

key_researchers.name: Jean-Sebastien Sottet
key_researchers.affiliation: Lead Researcher, Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST), Belvaux, Luxembourg
key_researchers.verification: Verified this session (LIST research profile, dblp)
key_researchers.connects_to: SQ3's silent-drift risk; the same institutional orbit as Cabot
key_researchers.why_relevant: Works on model-driven engineering, human-centred/'natural' modelling, model-driven digital twins and semantic drift; involved in the KONTEX workshop at MODELS 2026. Semantic drift is precisely the SQ3 failure mode where a stored judgment's meaning shifts as it is carried into a new context.

key_researchers.name: Martin Weyssow
key_researchers.affiliation: Research Scientist, Singapore Management University (Centre for Research on Intelligent Software Engineering); PhD at DIRO, Universite de Montreal under Houari Sahraoui
key_researchers.verification: Verified this session (personal site, FormaliSE 2026 profile)
key_researchers.connects_to: The Sahraoui/GEODES lineage of model-assistance mechanisms
key_researchers.why_relevant: His earlier work on recommendation and completion support during modelling activities is context for what 'assistance' meant in MDE before governance was added. His current line is LLMs for software vulnerability detection, which is off-thesis - read the modelling papers only.

key_researchers.name: Monique Snoeck
key_researchers.affiliation: Faculty of Economics and Business, KU Leuven, Belgium (Full Professor of Management Information Systems)
key_researchers.connects_to: The content of the judgment - the quality criteria an expert applies to a candidate model
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-author of Assessing the Suitability of LLMs in Generating UML Class Diagrams as Conceptual Models (EMMSAD 2025) and the authority on conceptual-model quality in the MERODE lineage. Supplies the quality criteria against which an expert is asked to judge, which is distinct from the trigger that asks them.

key_researchers.name: Roman Lukyanenko
key_researchers.affiliation: Associate Professor of Information Systems, McIntire School of Commerce, University of Virginia, USA
key_researchers.connects_to: SQ2 in reverse - curated human judgment governing the agentic system
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-authored Intelligent Agile: Conceptual Modeling and AI for Next-Generation Agile Software Development (HICSS 2026) WITH Arnon Sturm, so an existing supervisory connection exists. His Conceptual Modeling for Machine Learning line argues that domain knowledge in conceptual models should govern how ML is fed and constrained; his information-quality and crowdsourcing work also bears on validating stored judgments.

key_researchers.name: Veda C. Storey
key_researchers.affiliation: J. Mack Robinson College of Business, Georgia State University, USA
key_researchers.connects_to: Positioning the contribution within conceptual modelling rather than only within variability/SPL
key_researchers.why_relevant: Senior co-author of Conceptual Modeling: Topics, Themes, and Technology Trends (ACM Computing Surveys, 2023) and of the HICSS 2026 Intelligent Agile paper with Sturm. The field-level authority on where conceptual modelling research is heading. NOTE: venue, year and DOI of the CSUR survey are flagged Partial in the workbook - confirm before citing.

key_researchers.name: Marcello La Rosa
key_researchers.affiliation: Queensland University of Technology at the time of the 2017 survey; subsequently University of Melbourne (current affiliation uncertain)
key_researchers.connects_to: SQ3's cross-domain variability comparison; the safest analogue to clinical pathway variation
key_researchers.why_relevant: Lead author of Business Process Variability Modeling: A Survey (ACM Computing Surveys 2017). Provides the cross-domain variability evidence and comparison framework SQ3's transfer argument depends on, and is the closest analogue to clinical pathway variation that can be used now without any patient data or clinical claim.

key_researchers.name: Sebastian Gotz (with Uwe Assmann)
key_researchers.affiliation: TUD Dresden University of Technology, Faculty of Computer Science, Software Technology group, Germany
key_researchers.connects_to: The storage format of the human-judgment layer
key_researchers.why_relevant: Authors of Towards an Interoperable Model-driven Automated Assessment System for Computer Science Education (MODELS Companion 2024) - the closest existing work on portable representations for assessment artefacts, which is the substrate question underlying SQ2's 'how should judgment be stored'.

key_researchers.name: Alessio Ferrari (with Sallam Abualhaija and Chetan Arora)
key_researchers.affiliation: Associated with CNR-ISTI Pisa (Ferrari), SnT University of Luxembourg (Abualhaija) and Monash University (Arora) in prior work - none confirmed this session
key_researchers.connects_to: Cross-domain, cross-document-type reliability evidence for SQ3; a likely reviewer community
key_researchers.why_relevant: Authors of Model Generation with LLMs: From Requirements to UML Sequence Diagrams (REW 2024). Provides evidence about how LLM model generation behaves across domains and document types, which is the reliability baseline SQ3's transfer argument sits on. Also an active RE/LLM community likely to review the doctorate's outputs.

key_researchers.name: Ben Green
key_researchers.affiliation: University of Michigan, USA (previously Harvard, Berkman Klein Center)
key_researchers.tier: Tier 4 - BACKGROUND (but elevated in the read-first list)
key_researchers.connects_to: The honesty of the entire human-judgment layer claim; the word 'governed' in the umbrella RQ
key_researchers.why_relevant: The Principles and Limits of Algorithm-in-the-Loop Decision Making (CSCW 2019) and The flaws of policies requiring human oversight of government algorithms (CLSR 2022). His argument is that human-oversight mandates routinely fail to deliver real oversight. The U-RQ's promise to 'govern' human judgment is a promise to do better than the thing he shows does not work - so this is the standard the thesis sets for itself.

key_researchers.name: Been Kim
key_researchers.affiliation: Senior Staff Research Scientist, Google DeepMind, USA
key_researchers.connects_to: SQ2's representation problem; SQ3's silent concept drift
key_researchers.why_relevant: Her TCAV line expresses model behaviour in terms of human-defined concepts rather than raw features, and her recent 'neologism' argument is that human-machine communication needs new shared vocabulary. Substantial vs occasional is a human concept that must become machine-checkable without collapsing into a surface heuristic. Tier 4 rather than 2 because the thesis is unlikely to implement TCAV - read it for the framing.

key_researchers.name: Hilde Weerts
key_researchers.affiliation: Eindhoven University of Technology, Department of Mathematics and Computer Science, Netherlands
key_researchers.verification: Verified this session (institutional research profile); her specific human-oversight work NOT verified
key_researchers.connects_to: The regulatory framing around AI Act Article 14 (human oversight), which is already a verified source in the workbook
key_researchers.why_relevant: Works on algorithmic fairness in relation to EU non-discrimination law and the AI Act (Algorithmic Unfairness through the Lens of EU Non-Discrimination Law, FAccT 2023) and on Fairlearn. IF she has specific work operationalising Article 14 human-oversight requirements she moves to Tier 2 for the governance mechanism - verify before relying on that.

key_researchers.name: Percy Liang
key_researchers.affiliation: Stanford University, USA (uncertain - consistent with the cited papers but not confirmed this session)
key_researchers.connects_to: The human-judgment layer's retrieval design (via Generative Agents); SQ3's reporting convention (via WILDS)
key_researchers.why_relevant: His relevance is entirely through two large multi-author artifacts where he is senior author: WILDS (ICML 2021) and Generative Agents (UIST 2023), whose memory stream - retrieval scored by recency, importance and relevance, plus reflection - is the nearest published analogue of a human-judgment memory. Read the papers; do not treat him as a person-level match for this thesis.

sources.title: Not All Differences Matter: Variability Exploration of Domain Models via Agentic AI
sources.authors: Iris Reinhartz-Berger, Maxim Bragilovski, Arnon Sturm
sources.venue: ACM/IEEE 29th International Conference on Model Driven Engineering Languages and Systems (MODELS '26); DOI 10.1145/3822455.3830312
sources.why_read_first: READ FIRST. The framework everything is measured against - read it as the specification of what the thesis extends. WARNING: the public record is currently UNVERIFIED (DOI returned 404, ACM DL blocked automated access, not yet on the first author's dblp page). Most likely a timing artefact since MODELS 2026 runs 4-9 October 2026, but a human must confirm the final DOI and pages before citing.

sources.title: Towards Human-in-the-Loop LLM-Enabled Domain Modeling
sources.authors: Jonathan Silva Mercado, Qin Ma, Jordi Cabot, Pierre Kelsen, Henderik A. Proper
sources.venue: Conceptual Modeling - ER 2025, LNCS 16189, Springer, pp. 127-145; DOI 10.1007/978-3-032-08623-5_7
sources.why_read_first: READ SECOND. The closest published statement of SQ1's problem outside the supervisors' group. It supplies the architectural pattern SQ1 needs - a separate non-LLM arbiter with uncertainty-ranked question selection - but gives no policy for when to invoke the human at all. Treat as a competitor, not background.

sources.title: Iterative vs. Plan-Driven Approaches in Human-LLM Collaborative Modeling: An Empirical Study
sources.authors: Iris Reinhartz-Berger, Arava Tsoury
sources.venue: CAiSE 2026 (Advanced Information Systems Engineering), pp. 3-20; DOI 10.1007/978-3-032-28117-3_1
sources.why_read_first: READ THIRD. The supervisor's own baseline. It fixes the design space of when control passes between human and LLM but compares two fixed regimes rather than learning a policy - which is exactly the opening SQ1 must claim, and it cannot be omitted.

sources.title: Principles of Mixed-Initiative User Interfaces
sources.authors: Eric Horvitz
sources.venue: SIGCHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '99), Pittsburgh, pp. 159-166; DOI 10.1145/302979.303030
sources.why_read_first: READ EARLY, not as history. The expected-utility criterion for acting versus asking is the decision-theoretic argument SQ1's trigger must be derived from or explicitly argued against.

sources.title: Consistent Estimators for Learning to Defer to an Expert
sources.authors: Hussein Mozannar, David A. Sontag
sources.why_read_first: The concrete formalism and released code most likely to become SQ1's baseline. Read it specifically for what it assumes about the expert - those assumptions are where a modelling-assessment setting will break them.

sources.title: Is automated grading of models effective? Assessing automated grading of class diagrams
sources.authors: Weiyi Bian, Omar Alam, Jorg Kienzle
sources.venue: MODELS 2020 (23rd ACM/IEEE Int. Conf. on Model Driven Engineering Languages and Systems), pp. 365-376; DOI 10.1145/3365438.3410944
sources.why_read_first: The single-correct-answer assumption in its clearest form, on student class diagrams evaluated against real cohorts. This is the contrast case that makes the substantial-vs-occasional distinction load-bearing rather than decorative.

sources.title: Truth Is a Lie: Crowd Truth and the Seven Myths of Human Annotation
sources.authors: Lora Aroyo, Chris Welty
sources.venue: AI Magazine 36(1), pp. 15-24; DOI 10.1609/aimag.v36i1.2564
sources.why_read_first: Read BEFORE designing the EXP-005 label protocol, not after. It changes what 'a label' should be when two experts legitimately disagree about whether a difference is substantial or occasional.

sources.title: On the Utility of Domain Modeling Assistance with Large Language Models
sources.authors: Meriem Ben Chaaben, Lola Burgueno, Istvan David, Houari A. Sahraoui
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology (MAGDA); DOI 10.1145/3744920; preprint arXiv:2410.12577
sources.why_read_first: The evaluation design Study 1 should imitate - a rigorous user study of whether LLM modelling assistance actually helps - redirected from suggestion quality to intervention triggering.

sources.title: The flaws of policies requiring human oversight of government algorithms
sources.authors: Ben Green
sources.venue: Computer Law & Security Review, volume 45
sources.why_read_first: The strongest available argument that mandated 'human oversight' is usually theatre. Read it as the standard the word 'governed' in the umbrella research question commits the thesis to meeting.

sources.title: WILDS: A Benchmark of in-the-Wild Distribution Shifts
sources.authors: Pang Wei Koh, Shiori Sagawa, et al. (23 authors, incl. Percy Liang)
sources.venue: ICML 2021, PMLR 139
sources.why_read_first: Gives SQ3 its in-distribution vs out-of-distribution reporting convention and the domain-generalization / subpopulation-shift split - the vocabulary that makes the required domain-specific vs broadly-transferable distinction operational rather than rhetorical.

sources.title: Generative AI And Software Variability - A Research Vision
sources.authors: Sandra Greiner, Klaus Schmid, Thorsten Berger, Sebastian Krieter, Kristof Meixner
sources.venue: 18th Int. Working Conference on Variability Modelling of Software-Intensive Systems (VaMoS 2024), Bern; DOI 10.1145/3634713.3634722
sources.why_read_first: The variability community's own statement of the open agenda at the generative-AI intersection. Cite it so the gap addressed by SQ2 and SQ3 is theirs rather than self-declared.

sources.title: A Design Science Research Methodology for Information Systems Research
sources.authors: Ken Peffers, Tuure Tuunanen, Marcus A. Rothenberger, Samir Chatterjee
sources.venue: Journal of Management Information Systems 24(3), pp. 45-77
sources.why_read_first: The process model that structures Chapter 4 and the three sub-question iterations. Read alongside FEDS (Venable, Pries-Heje & Baskerville, EJIS 2016) for the evaluation-strategy vocabulary that makes each study design defensible.

sources.title: FEDS: a Framework for Evaluation in Design Science Research
sources.authors: John Venable, Jan Pries-Heje, Richard Baskerville
sources.venue: European Journal of Information Systems 25(1), pp. 77-89
sources.why_read_first: Pairs with Peffers. The Human Risk & Effectiveness evaluation strategy is the one that fits a human-judgment governance artifact, and it justifies an evaluation design that does not rest on a single accuracy number.

sources.title: Beyond Grading Accuracy: Exploring Alignment of TAs and LLMs
sources.authors: Matthijs Jansen op de Haar, Nacir Bouali, Faizan Ahmed
sources.venue: arXiv:2603.16357 (v1 17 March 2026, v2 17 June 2026); publication venue unknown
sources.why_read_first: NEW - found and verified on arXiv in this session, not yet in the literature workbook. Criterion-level comparison of six open-source LLMs against teaching-assistant grades on 92 UML class diagrams, framed explicitly as support for mixed-initiative grading with instructor oversight. Close to SQ1; add to the workbook and check whether it has been formally published.

sources.title: Is generalisation hindering the adoption of your findings?
sources.authors: Rogardt Heldal
sources.venue: 18th ACM/IEEE Int. Symposium on Empirical Software Engineering and Measurement (ESEM 2024), pp. 348-358; DOI 10.1145/3674805.3686694
sources.why_read_first: Just outside the top twelve but important: the closest published counter-position to SQ3's default assumption, based on a failed variability-management artifact across five organisations. Cite it against yourself before an examiner does.

sources.title: Design Science Methodology for Information Systems and Software Engineering
sources.authors: Roel J. Wieringa
sources.venue: Springer, Berlin/Heidelberg (book); ISBN 978-3-662-43838-1
sources.why_read_first: Just outside the top twelve. His design-problem vs knowledge-question split is the sharpest tool available for the supervisor requirement to separate the proposed agentic solution from the research question.

sources.title: Research Perspectives: The Anatomy of a Design Principle
sources.authors: Shirley Gregor, Leona Chandra Kruse, Stefan Seidel
sources.venue: Journal of the Association for Information Systems 21, pp. 1622-1652; DOI 10.17705/1jais.00649
sources.why_read_first: Just outside the top twelve. A ready-made schema for storing reusable expert judgment WITH explicit boundary conditions, which is precisely SQ2's 'without unsafe generalization' clause. Note: the issue number is unconfirmed in the workbook and the second author's name appears in two forms.

sources.title: Can Multimodal Large Language Models Grade Like an Expert? A Study on UML Class Diagram Assessment Accuracy
sources.authors: Maria Blanca Ibanez, Maria Lucia Barron-Estrada, Ramon Zatarain-Cabada
sources.venue: Computer Applications in Engineering Education 33(5), article e70080; DOI 10.1002/cae.70080
sources.why_read_first: The most usable empirical justification for escalating on semantic interpretation and evaluative reasoning rather than on syntax - i.e. evidence about WHICH failure class the SQ1 trigger should be tuned to catch.

sources.title: Towards Multi-Agentic AI for automated software design and modelling: challenges and opportunities
sources.authors: Hoa Khanh Dam
sources.venue: ASEW 2025 (IEEE/ACM ASE Workshops), MAS-GAIN workshop, Seoul, pp. 311-314; DOI 10.1109/ASEW67777.2025.00063
sources.why_read_first: The clearest EXTERNAL statement of the SQ2 gap: it explicitly names conflict and inconsistency reconciliation across agent-produced design models as an open challenge. Cite it so the gap is community-recognised.

sources.title: Robots That Ask For Help: Uncertainty Alignment for Large Language Model Planners
sources.authors: Allen Z. Ren, Anushri Dixit, et al. (14 authors, senior author Anirudha Majumdar)
sources.venue: Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL 2023), PMLR 229, pp. 661-682; arXiv:2307.01928
sources.why_read_first: The closest existing end-to-end template for SQ1 in a different application domain: conformal-prediction-calibrated help-seeking with an explicitly minimised help rate and a task-success guarantee.
